insights: Leading digit characterization: p | gcd(a_n, L_n) iff p | numerator(H_k) where k = leading digit of n in base p
General family: for any prime p >= 3, (p-1)*p^k has leading digit p-1, so p | gcd for these n
Sum of inverses mod p is zero: follows from k -> k^(-1) being a bijection on units
GCD values for n=1..10: 1,1,1,1,1,3,3,3,1,1 - first gcd>1 at n=6, returns to 1 at n=9
n=6,7,8 all have gcd=3 because their leading digit in base 3 is 2 = 3-1
Second infinite family {4*5^k} gives infinitely many n with 5 | gcd
Part 1 (gcd=1 infinitely often) remains OPEN - requires understanding correlations across primes
